question: What was the primary outcome definition and modeling horizon used in this study?
reference_answer: The primary outcome, termed ‘incident AF’, included new-onset AF or atrial flutter, and incident AF at 5 years was modelled as a binary outcome.
acceptable_answers: incident AF included new-onset AF or atrial flutter; incident AF at 5 years modelled as binary outcome

question: What deep learning architecture and ECG input characteristics were used for the ECG-AI model?
reference_answer: The ECG-AI model was a single ResNet-50 initialized with random weights; it receives a single 12-lead ECG as input, with a duration of 10 s per lead at a sampling rate of 250 Hz.
acceptable_answers: single ResNet-50 with random initialization; single 12-lead ECG; 10 s per lead; 250 Hz

question: How were hyperparameters optimized and the best ECG-AI model selected during training?
reference_answer: Hyperparameters were optimized on the validation set using a Bayesian grid-search approach, and the best performing model in the validation set was selected based on the lowest loss.
acceptable_answers: Bayesian grid-search on validation set; best model selected by lowest validation loss

question: In the MHI Biobank comparison, what AUC-ROC values were reported for ECG-AI, AF-PGS, and CHARGE-AF?
reference_answer: ECG-AI had an AUC-ROC of .76 (95% CI: .74–.79); AF-PGS had an AUC-ROC of .59 (95% CI: .57–.63); CHARGE-AF had an AUC-ROC of .62 (95% CI: .60–.65).
acceptable_answers: ECG-AI AUC-ROC of .76; AF-PGS AUC-ROC of .59; CHARGE-AF AUC-ROC of .62

question: In the MHI All-Comers test set, at a classification threshold of 12%, what sensitivity, specificity, and negative predictive value did the ECG-AI model show at the patient level?
reference_answer: At a classification threshold of 12%, the ECG-AI model showed a sensitivity of 66%, a specificity of 75%, and a negative predictive value of 93% at the patient level.

question: Which page and section report that adding AF-PGS and/or CHARGE-AF to ECG-AI improved calibration in the MHI Biobank group, and what ECI reduction was reported for ‘ECG-AI + AF-PGS’ compared with ‘ECG-AI alone’?
reference_answer: This is reported on page 8 in the section ‘Atrial fibrillation prediction in MHI Biobank patients using ECG-based deep learning, AF-PGS, and CHARGE-AF’. The ECI was reduced from .157 (95% CI: .125–.198) for ‘ECG-AI alone’ to .095 (95% CI: .052–.147) for ‘ECG-AI + AF-PGS’.

question: Across the MHI All-Comers and MHI Biobank analyses, what pattern is described when clinical variables or polygenic scores are added to ECG-AI as post-training LR models, particularly regarding discrimination versus calibration/fit?
reference_answer: In MHI All-Comers, adding age and sex to ECG-AI yielded a similar AUC-ROC (.75) and did not provide an overall better fit (LRT statistic < 0, P = 1). In MHI Biobank, adding AF-PGS and/or CHARGE-AF to ECG-AI yielded similar AUC-ROC compared with ECG-AI, but improved calibration (ECI reduction) and overall fit (P = .0002 for ‘ECG-AI + AF-PGS’; P < .0001 for ‘ECG-AI + AF-PGS + CHARGE-AF’). Thus the described pattern is minimal discrimination change with better calibration/fit for some added variables in the Biobank setting.
acceptable_answers: similar AUC-ROC but improved calibration/fit in MHI Biobank; no better fit for age and sex in MHI All-Comers
